canonical_definition: Instruction Following is the ability of large language models (LLMs) to interpret and execute explicit natural language instructions to generate task-specific responses or structured outputs, often enhanced through instruction tuning or alignment processes. This capability involves adhering to constraints (e.g., format, rules, complexity) and is critical for aligning model behavior with human intentions across single-turn, multi-turn, and multimodal settings. While some definitions emphasize sensitivity to prompt engineering and explicit task induction, others highlight its role in enabling controllability, structured output generation, or performance in long-horizon tasks, with variations in scope depending on application domains (e.g., robotics, code generation, vision-language tasks).
